item.title: Claude Code vs Cursor: How Each One Remembers Your Project (2026)
item.description:
Claude Code vs Cursor: which one remembers more?

Both tools read instruction files at the start of a session, so both can carry project rules across chats. The difference is who writes the memory. Claude Code can save its own notes (auto memory) on top of the files you write. Cursor’s documented memory is the rules you write: project rules, AGENTS.md and user rules. Cursor’s rules page says large language models do not keep memory between completions, so rules are what persist.

item.title: Codex vs Cursor: How Each One Remembers Your Project (2026)
item.description:
Codex vs Cursor: which one remembers more?

Both tools read instruction files at the start of work, so both can carry project rules from one chat to the next. The difference is who writes the memory. Codex can save notes from past chats in local memory files, if you turn that on. Cursor’s documented memory is the rules you write: project rules, AGENTS.md and user rules. Cursor’s rules page says large language models do not keep memory between completions, so rules are what persist.

item.title: Cursor Rules: .mdc Files, AGENTS.md and Memory (2026)
item.description:
Cursor rules are instruction files that Cursor adds to the agent’s context. You write them once, and Cursor reads them in later chats. Project rules are .mdc files in .cursor/rules, which Cursor’s docs say is version-controlled and scoped to the codebase. Cursor also reads AGENTS.md files, and it has User and Team rules for wider scopes.

This page covers the rule types, how each one is applied, and where Hindsight fits for Cursor users. For a side-by-side with Claude Code’s files, see Claude Code vs Cursor, and for Codex’s files see Codex vs Cursor. Facts come from Cursor’s rules docs (read 2026-11-15) and Hindsight’s coding agents page (read 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-15).

item.title: AI Coding Agent Memory: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and More
item.description: AI coding agent memory is how tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot carry project knowledge from one session to the next. The main mechanism is a plain instruction file (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or Cursor rules) loaded into every session. Some agents add automatic memory that saves lessons as they work. For more, teams add an external memory server. For Claude Code specifically, see Claude Code memory. For how popular each agent is (GitHub stars, npm and PyPI downloads), see AI coding agent statistics.
